question: A 20-year-old girl presents to a physician following unprotected coitus with her boyfriend about 10 hours ago. She tells the doctor that although they usually use a barrier method of contraception, this time they forgot. She does not want to become pregnant. She also mentions that she has major depression and does not want to take an estrogen-containing pill. After necessary counseling, the physician prescribes an enteric-coated pill containing 1.5 mg of levonorgestrel. Which of the following is the primary mechanism of action of this drug?

options.opa: Reduction in motility of cilia in the fallopian tubes
options.opb: Mucosal hypertrophy and polyp formation in cervix
options.opd: Delayed ovulation through inhibition of follicular development

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Levonorgestrel -> Inhibition of follicular development -> Delayed ovulation -> 95% CHAIN: Levonorgestrel -> Thickening of cervical mucus -> Impaired sperm penetration -> 90% CHAIN: Levonorgestrel -> Atrophy of the endometrium -> Impaired implantation -> 95%
analysis: Levonorgestrel is a progestin-only emergency contraceptive pill. Its primary mechanism of action is to prevent pregnancy by delaying or inhibiting ovulation. It may also alter the cervical mucus to inhibit sperm penetration and reduce the likelihood of fertilization.
